```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## 1. Aim

Fit five Birnbaum–Saunders (BS)-family models to daily ozone readings by maximum
likelihood, compare them with AIC, BIC and the Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS) test, and plot
the fitted curves over the data.

| Model | Description |
|---|---|
| BS | Standard two-parameter Birnbaum–Saunders |
| Log-GBS | Generalised BS with a logistic parent distribution |
| t-BS | Student's-t BS (extra parameter: degrees of freedom) |
| Delta-BS | Power-exponent generalisation of BS (delta = 1 gives the ordinary BS) |
| KM-BS | BS passed through the Kavya–Manoharan transformation |

**Note on the density:** for the BS-type models, the density of x is
f(x) = g(z) * (x + beta) / (2 * alpha * x * sqrt(x * beta)), where
z = (sqrt(x/beta) - sqrt(beta/x)) / alpha and g is the parent density
(normal, logistic or Student's-t). This is the form used below.

## 2. Load and clean the data

Keep the data file in the same folder as this .Rmd file. To run another city,
change `data_file` and `city_name` and knit again.

```{r load-data}
data_file <- "D:/winter semester/Statistical Inference lab/O3 dataset.xlsx"  # file name only (no D:/ path)
city_name <- "Ahmedabad"         # used in plot titles and output file names

if (grepl("\\.csv$", data_file, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
  raw <- read.csv(data_file)
} else {
  library(readxl)
  raw <- read_excel(data_file)
}

x_all <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(raw[[1]]))
x <- x_all[!is.na(x_all) & x_all > 0]   # BS-type models need x > 0
n <- length(x)

cat("Observations read:", length(x_all), "\n")
cat("Kept (non-missing and positive):", n, "\n")
summary(x)
```

## 3. Model functions

```{r model-functions}
# ---------- common pieces ----------
z_bs <- function(x, alpha, beta) (1 / alpha) * (sqrt(x / beta) - sqrt(beta / x))

# log of the Jacobian term (x + beta) / (2 * alpha * x * sqrt(x * beta))
log_jac_bs <- function(x, alpha, beta) {
  log(x + beta) - log(2 * alpha) - 1.5 * log(x) - 0.5 * log(beta)
}

BAD <- 1e10   # returned when parameters are invalid

# ---------- 1. Birnbaum-Saunders (BS) ----------
cdf_bs <- function(x, alpha, beta) pnorm(z_bs(x, alpha, beta))
pdf_bs <- function(x, alpha, beta) {
  dnorm(z_bs(x, alpha, beta)) * exp(log_jac_bs(x, alpha, beta))
}
loglik_bs <- function(par, x) {
  alpha <- par[1]; beta <- par[2]
  if (alpha <= 0 || beta <= 0) return(BAD)
  logpdf <- dnorm(z_bs(x, alpha, beta), log = TRUE) + log_jac_bs(x, alpha, beta)
  if (any(!is.finite(logpdf))) return(BAD)
  -sum(logpdf)
}

# ---------- 2. Logistic-GBS (Log-GBS) ----------
cdf_lgbs <- function(x, alpha, beta) plogis(z_bs(x, alpha, beta))
pdf_lgbs <- function(x, alpha, beta) {
  dlogis(z_bs(x, alpha, beta)) * exp(log_jac_bs(x, alpha, beta))
}
loglik_lgbs <- function(par, x) {
  alpha <- par[1]; beta <- par[2]
  if (alpha <= 0 || beta <= 0) return(BAD)
  logpdf <- dlogis(z_bs(x, alpha, beta), log = TRUE) + log_jac_bs(x, alpha, beta)
  if (any(!is.finite(logpdf))) return(BAD)
  -sum(logpdf)
}

# ---------- 3. Student-t BS (t-BS) ----------
cdf_tbs <- function(x, alpha, beta, nu) pt(z_bs(x, alpha, beta), df = nu)
pdf_tbs <- function(x, alpha, beta, nu) {
  dt(z_bs(x, alpha, beta), df = nu) * exp(log_jac_bs(x, alpha, beta))
}
loglik_tbs <- function(par, x) {
  alpha <- par[1]; beta <- par[2]; nu <- par[3]
  if (alpha <= 0 || beta <= 0 || nu <= 1) return(BAD)
  logpdf <- dt(z_bs(x, alpha, beta), df = nu, log = TRUE) + log_jac_bs(x, alpha, beta)
  if (any(!is.finite(logpdf))) return(BAD)
  -sum(logpdf)
}

# ---------- 4. Delta-BS (power-exponent generalisation) ----------
z_delta <- function(x, alpha, beta, delta) {
  (1 / alpha) * ((x / beta)^(delta / 2) - (beta / x)^(delta / 2))
}
jac_delta <- function(x, alpha, beta, delta) {
  (delta / (2 * alpha)) *
    (beta^(-delta / 2) * x^(delta / 2 - 1) + beta^(delta / 2) * x^(-(delta / 2 + 1)))
}
cdf_delta_bs <- function(x, alpha, beta, delta) pnorm(z_delta(x, alpha, beta, delta))
pdf_delta_bs <- function(x, alpha, beta, delta) {
  dnorm(z_delta(x, alpha, beta, delta)) * jac_delta(x, alpha, beta, delta)
}
loglik_delta <- function(par, x) {
  alpha <- par[1]; beta <- par[2]; delta <- par[3]
  if (alpha <= 0 || beta <= 0 || delta <= 0) return(BAD)
  logpdf <- dnorm(z_delta(x, alpha, beta, delta), log = TRUE) +
    log(jac_delta(x, alpha, beta, delta))
  if (any(!is.finite(logpdf))) return(BAD)
  -sum(logpdf)
}

# ---------- 5. KM-BS (Kavya-Manoharan transformation of BS) ----------
km_const <- exp(1) / (exp(1) - 1)
cdf_kmbs <- function(x, alpha, beta) km_const * (1 - exp(-cdf_bs(x, alpha, beta)))
pdf_kmbs <- function(x, alpha, beta) {
  km_const * exp(-cdf_bs(x, alpha, beta)) * pdf_bs(x, alpha, beta)
}
loglik_kmbs <- function(par, x) {
  alpha <- par[1]; beta <- par[2]
  if (alpha <= 0 || beta <= 0) return(BAD)
  G <- cdf_bs(x, alpha, beta)
  logpdf <- log(km_const) - G +
    dnorm(z_bs(x, alpha, beta), log = TRUE) + log_jac_bs(x, alpha, beta)
  if (any(!is.finite(logpdf))) return(BAD)
  -sum(logpdf)
}
```

## 4. Starting values

Modified-moment estimates for the BS model are used as starting points
(s = arithmetic mean, r = harmonic mean).

```{r start-values}
s <- mean(x)
r <- 1 / mean(1 / x)
alpha0 <- sqrt(2 * (sqrt(s / r) - 1))
beta0  <- sqrt(s * r)
if (!is.finite(alpha0) || alpha0 < 0.05) alpha0 <- 0.5

c(alpha0 = alpha0, beta0 = beta0)
```

## 5. Maximum likelihood fitting

Each model is fitted from several starting points and the best result is kept.

```{r fit}
fit_model <- function(fn, starts, lower, x) {
  fits <- lapply(starts, function(s0) {
    tryCatch(optim(s0, fn, x = x, method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = lower),
             error = function(e) NULL)
  })
  fits <- Filter(Negate(is.null), fits)
  fits <- Filter(function(f) is.finite(f$value) && f$value < BAD / 10, fits)
  if (length(fits) == 0) stop("No valid fit found for this model.")
  fits[[which.min(sapply(fits, function(f) f$value))]]
}

eps <- 1e-8
starts2   <- list(c(alpha0, beta0), c(1, median(x)), c(0.5, median(x)))
starts3_t <- lapply(starts2, function(s0) c(s0, 5))
starts3_d <- lapply(starts2, function(s0) c(s0, 1))

fit_bs    <- fit_model(loglik_bs,    starts2,   c(eps, eps),       x)
fit_lgbs  <- fit_model(loglik_lgbs,  starts2,   c(eps, eps),       x)
fit_tbs   <- fit_model(loglik_tbs,   starts3_t, c(eps, eps, 1.01), x)
fit_delta <- fit_model(loglik_delta, starts3_d, c(eps, eps, eps),  x)
fit_kmbs  <- fit_model(loglik_kmbs,  starts2,   c(eps, eps),       x)

# 0 = the optimiser reports convergence
c(BS = fit_bs$convergence, LogGBS = fit_lgbs$convergence, tBS = fit_tbs$convergence,
  DeltaBS = fit_delta$convergence, KMBS = fit_kmbs$convergence)
```

## 6. Model selection: AIC, BIC and KS test

```{r criteria}
AIC_manual <- function(nll, k) 2 * k + 2 * nll
BIC_manual <- function(nll, k, n) log(n) * k + 2 * nll

fits <- list(BS = fit_bs, `t-BS` = fit_tbs, `Delta-BS` = fit_delta,
             `Log-GBS` = fit_lgbs, `KM-BS` = fit_kmbs)

aic <- sapply(fits, function(f) AIC_manual(f$value, length(f$par)))
bic <- sapply(fits, function(f) BIC_manual(f$value, length(f$par), n))

# KS test (a tiny jitter breaks ties in rounded measurements)
set.seed(101)
x_j <- jitter(x, amount = 1e-6)
ks <- list(
  BS         = ks.test(x_j, function(y) cdf_bs(y, fit_bs$par[1], fit_bs$par[2])),
  `t-BS`     = ks.test(x_j, function(y) cdf_tbs(y, fit_tbs$par[1], fit_tbs$par[2], fit_tbs$par[3])),
  `Delta-BS` = ks.test(x_j, function(y) cdf_delta_bs(y, fit_delta$par[1], fit_delta$par[2], fit_delta$par[3])),
  `Log-GBS`  = ks.test(x_j, function(y) cdf_lgbs(y, fit_lgbs$par[1], fit_lgbs$par[2])),
  `KM-BS`    = ks.test(x_j, function(y) cdf_kmbs(y, fit_kmbs$par[1], fit_kmbs$par[2]))
)
```

## 7. Comparison table

```{r results-table}
results <- data.frame(
  Model       = names(fits),
  Alpha       = sapply(fits, function(f) f$par[1]),
  Beta        = sapply(fits, function(f) f$par[2]),
  Extra_Param = sapply(fits, function(f) if (length(f$par) > 2) f$par[3] else NA),
  AIC         = aic,
  BIC         = bic,
  KS_Statistic = sapply(ks, function(k) unname(k$statistic)),
  KS_p_value   = sapply(ks, function(k) k$p.value),
  Converged    = sapply(fits, function(f) f$convergence == 0),
  row.names = NULL
)
num_cols <- c("Alpha", "Beta", "Extra_Param", "AIC", "BIC", "KS_Statistic", "KS_p_value")
results[, num_cols] <- round(results[, num_cols], 6)

knitr::kable(results,
  caption = paste("Comparison of Birnbaum–Saunders models:", city_name, "ozone"))

cat("Lowest AIC:", results$Model[which.min(results$AIC)], "\n")
cat("Lowest BIC:", results$Model[which.min(results$BIC)], "\n")

dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(results, file.path("results", paste0("comparison_", tolower(city_name), ".csv")),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

## 8. Plots

```{r plots, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
cols <- c(BS = "blue", `Log-GBS` = "red", `t-BS` = "darkgreen",
          `Delta-BS` = "purple", `KM-BS` = "orange")
ltys <- c(BS = 1, `Log-GBS` = 2, `t-BS` = 3, `Delta-BS` = 4, `KM-BS` = 5)
xs <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 1000)

plot_pdf_fits <- function() {
  h <- hist(x, breaks = 40, plot = FALSE)
  plot(h, freq = FALSE, ylim = c(0, max(h$density) * 1.6),
       col = "grey90", border = "white",
       main = paste("Ozone:", city_name, "- histogram with fitted distributions"),
       xlab = "Ozone concentration", ylab = "Density")
  lines(xs, pdf_bs(xs, fit_bs$par[1], fit_bs$par[2]), col = cols["BS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["BS"])
  lines(xs, pdf_lgbs(xs, fit_lgbs$par[1], fit_lgbs$par[2]), col = cols["Log-GBS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["Log-GBS"])
  lines(xs, pdf_tbs(xs, fit_tbs$par[1], fit_tbs$par[2], fit_tbs$par[3]), col = cols["t-BS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["t-BS"])
  lines(xs, pdf_delta_bs(xs, fit_delta$par[1], fit_delta$par[2], fit_delta$par[3]), col = cols["Delta-BS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["Delta-BS"])
  lines(xs, pdf_kmbs(xs, fit_kmbs$par[1], fit_kmbs$par[2]), col = cols["KM-BS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["KM-BS"])
  legend("topright", legend = names(cols), col = cols, lty = ltys, lwd = 2, bty = "n")
}

plot_cdf_fits <- function() {
  plot(ecdf(x), do.points = FALSE, verticals = TRUE, col = "grey40", lwd = 2,
       main = paste("Ozone:", city_name, "- empirical vs fitted CDF"),
       xlab = "Ozone concentration", ylab = "Cumulative probability")
  lines(xs, cdf_bs(xs, fit_bs$par[1], fit_bs$par[2]), col = cols["BS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["BS"])
  lines(xs, cdf_lgbs(xs, fit_lgbs$par[1], fit_lgbs$par[2]), col = cols["Log-GBS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["Log-GBS"])
  lines(xs, cdf_tbs(xs, fit_tbs$par[1], fit_tbs$par[2], fit_tbs$par[3]), col = cols["t-BS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["t-BS"])
  lines(xs, cdf_delta_bs(xs, fit_delta$par[1], fit_delta$par[2], fit_delta$par[3]), col = cols["Delta-BS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["Delta-BS"])
  lines(xs, cdf_kmbs(xs, fit_kmbs$par[1], fit_kmbs$par[2]), col = cols["KM-BS"], lwd = 2, lty = ltys["KM-BS"])
  legend("bottomright", legend = c("Empirical", names(cols)),
         col = c("grey40", cols), lty = c(1, ltys), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
}

plot_pdf_fits()
plot_cdf_fits()

# Save the plots as PNG files for GitHub
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
png(file.path("figures", paste0("ozone_", tolower(city_name), "_pdf_fit.png")),
    width = 1000, height = 700, res = 120)
plot_pdf_fits()
dev.off()
png(file.path("figures", paste0("ozone_", tolower(city_name), "_cdf_fit.png")),
    width = 1000, height = 700, res = 120)
plot_cdf_fits()
dev.off()
```

## 9. How to read the results

- Lower AIC and BIC mean a better balance of fit and simplicity.
- A smaller KS statistic and a larger p-value mean the fitted CDF is closer to the data.
  With very large samples the KS test rejects almost every model, so compare the
  statistics as well as the p-values.
- Check the `Converged` column and the plots before drawing any conclusion. A fitted
  curve that sits far from the histogram means the fit should not be trusted.
